ai.title: Many languages, one common neural code
ai.brief: Languages take on thousands of forms. Some are tonal, like Vietnamese, where shifts in pitch convey distinct meanings. English relies on precise word orders, but this matters less for Russian, where words can be swapped without changing the intended message. Despite so much variety in the linguistic kingdom, an MIT study has found that the human brain may process all sorts of languages in a universal way. Artificial intelligence made this finding possible. In the study published today in Nature Neuroscience , the researchers used multilingual models to predict how the human brain responds to various languages. Those models also helped the researchers detect a shared brain process across people who collectively spoke 21 different languages. “Of course, there are many differences in the ways humans converse with each other.

sec.title: Hackers May Have Breached FBI Database Used by Police Nationwide
sec.brief: S. S. CISA adds Apache Axis, Vanderbilt REDCap,BerriAI LiteLLM, and Synology DSM flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog The FBI is investigating a possible breach of a database that police use to check arrest warrants and access criminal records. According to the BBC , US media reported the incident, citing two people familiar with the matter. The FBI has not publicly commented on the reports and did not respond to the BBC’s request for comment. The database is the National Crime Information Center (NCIC). Federal and local law enforcement agencies use it to share information about arrest warrants and background checks. Police officers also access it during traffic stops and investigations. According to the FBI, as of 2023, the NCIC contained more than 18 million active records across 22 databases and provided services to over 100,000 law enforcement and criminal justice organisations.
